# Gold mine report: 'Ask HN: What's your current AI agentic setup?'

Thread: HN item 50366117, 645 comments. Source: eight reader chunks, merged and de-duplicated here. Comment ids are cited as [#id]. Model names, prices and usage figures are as commenters reported them. None of them are verified. This synthesis step made no repository changes and no nested model calls.

## 1. The short version

- **Cross-vendor review is the pattern with the most support.** At least a dozen independent setups have one provider write and another review, by default [#50370886] [#50373001] [#50378365] [#50389282] [#50376463]. John's harness already works this way. Keep it and sharpen it.
- **'Plan strong, execute cheap' is a close second**, ideally with escalation when the cheap tier fails [#50374549] [#50378856] [#50375921]. John's three model routes already follow this pattern. The missing piece is an explicit, logged escalation step.
- **Memory belongs in files, not in the context window.** That means HANDOFF.md resets, ADRs, state files and close-out notes [#50375342] [#50376262] [#50377952] [#50375278].
- **The minimalists make a lot of noise and are often right.** Newer models need fewer guardrails [#50378434] [#50379944]. But almost nobody tests a custom setup against the vanilla harness [#50379514]. That test is John's best next experiment.
- **Cheap open models are now very cheap, and there is real data to show it** [#50381117] [#50375427] [#50385251]. But models still write poor prose [#50367589] [#50373357] [#50375084]. For a content harness this backs the current split: GreenPT does bounded extraction, and the strong owners do the prose and the judgement.
- **Wide swarms, personal 'claw' agents and local inference are mostly noise for this setup.**

## 2. How the scores work

Every item gets four scores, each from 1 to 5. The total is out of 20.
- **Impact:** how much it would improve results.
- **Ease:** how cheap it is to adopt.
- **Evidence:** how many independent commenters back it, and how specific or data-backed they are.
- **Fit:** how well it suits John's harness: three providers, GitHub task packets, receipts, budget caps, review reuse, work from a phone, and content consumers (the chauffeur academy and the Sark retreat site).

## 4. Camp by camp

### 4.1 Cross-vendor review (19)
This is the most common serious pattern in the thread.
- **Author with one vendor, review with another.** Opus writes and Codex reviews by default, with Grok and Gemini added for critical work [#50370886]. Codex Pro works as the second-opinion reviewer [#50373001]. Opus is reviewed by GPT Sol, with both on $20 plans [#50373589]. navels built neal so that Codex reviews Claude or the other way round [#50373463].
- **Calling the reviewer.** Some call Codex's review function from inside the Claude CLI [#50378365]. Others run Codex as a pre-PR or post-PR hook [#50376390]. One person pays for a cheap third subscription purely for adversarial review [#50377705].
- **Why it works.** In glennfiedler's words, 'each model sees things the others don't' [#50375606]. Even a skeptic finds real bugs with 'now review this' [#50380787].
- **Sharper variants.**
  - A fresh session reviews with a fixed list of 16 of your own PR questions [#50378899].
  - Implementer and clean-context reviewer loops repeat until no serious issue remains [#50379808].
  - Reviews are cached and pinned to the commit hash, and an AST-diff after a rebase decides whether a review can be reused [#50378157]. This is close to John's rule 11.
- **The warning.** AI review almost always finds something, even straight after you fix the last round [#50374732]. You need a stop rule.

### 4.2 Tiered routing (19)
- **Plan strong, execute cheap.** Opus plans and Sonnet executes [#50374549]. Claude files issues and OpenCode with DeepSeek picks them up [#50373974]. oh-my-pi's 'prewalk' pairs an Opus planner with a DeepSeek executor [#50376454]. Claude ($20) plans, Codex ($20) reviews and DeepSeek ($1-3 a day) implements, all for under $100 a month [#50378856]. Opus plans and reviews, Sonnet writes code and Haiku does the mechanical work [#50389538].
- **Escalation.** An Opus coordinator puts each card in a tier: flash, pro, heavy or frontier. A card that fails moves up a tier [#50375921]. Others use the top model only when stuck or on a high-value step [#50374502], or only for big-picture planning [#50381009].
- **Raise effort only where it pays.** Use it for architecture work, and split implementation into small pieces that need low reasoning [#50367589].
- **For John.** The routes exist already. Make escalation a recorded event on the receipt, triggered by a failed deterministic check, not by judgement.

### 4.3 Context and memory as files (19)
- **Reset instead of compacting.** The agent writes HANDOFF.md, listing the subtasks, their status, what was learnt and what remains. Then a fresh agent starts from it [#50375342].
- **A memory folder in version control.** bottom999mottob keeps LOG.md, HANDOFF.md and DECISIONS.md plus a plan folder [#50375274].
- **ADRs written as the project goes.** stkni found they 'raised overall output quality' [#50376262] [#50376451].
- **A shared-memory repo with rules and state.** There is one rules file (especially what is forbidden) and one state file per repo. Each task has an Org-mode file naming its owner agent and model. Hooks keep it all current [#50377952].
- **A close-out routine.** At the end of a session, the agent writes hints into AGENTS.md [#50375278].
- **A full trace.** A 'status repo' records everything, but it eats tokens [#50375619].
- **Keep context small.** Keep the context window under 10% full and start fresh from markdown [#50375856].
- **The contrarian.** Re-explaining forces better thinking about architecture [#50376204]. The answer is to keep these files short, not to drop them.

### 4.4 Minimalism and evals against vanilla (18)
- **Plain setups go a long way.** Many people run plain Claude Code or Codex and stop there [#50373208] [#50380407] [#50375079].
- **Complex setups age fast.** 'Almost all of the intelligence is in the model', so complex setups are obsolete within months [#50373351].
- **Newer models need less scaffolding.** Since the 5.5 models arrived, they 'need less skills and guardrails' [#50378434]. Organisation structures need less attention as models improve [#50379944].
- **Broad context hurts.** Broad skills and tool access poison the context [#50380583]. One commenter added a switch that ignores bloated repo instructions [#50375302].
- **The sharpest point.** 'All of these gas towns and no one running evals to compare to the vanilla harness' [#50379514].
- **Ways to compare.** Use a locked-down baseline harness [#50375145]. Or benchmark on your own past sessions rather than leaderboards [#50378628].
- **For John.** His ~19-rule CLAUDE.md is exactly what this camp would challenge. The fair answer is a bake-off, not a debate.

### 4.5 Issues and tickets as the interface (18)
- **GitHub issues as the hand-off.** One person says this is 'simple and resilient enough' [#50373974]. claudeflow turns issues into Claude one-shots and handles CI and landing the PR [#50374380]. A Pi GitHub Action runs an issue-and-PR workflow [#50374094].
- **Tickets as the conversation.** jiraude makes tickets the whole interface. Questions come back in the ticket, and side findings become new tickets [#50376058] [#50384746].
- **Kanban as plain files.** Kan keeps cards as files in the repo, with dependencies and a `kan ready` query [#50374498].
- **For John.** He already works this way. The thread confirms it is a strong design, not over-engineering.

### 4.6 Deterministic-first workflows (17)
- **Promote what works.** Start a workflow as a skill and make it deterministic once it proves useful [#50367326]. When you need throughput, automate the deterministic parts first [#50367587].
- **Scripts first, agents as fallback.** poelzi runs 40+ step workflows that are mostly scripts, with agents only as fallbacks. Each failure hardens the workflow, and runs can resume [#50378157].
- **Turn token sinks into code.** When Fordec hits his weekly limit, he studies his consumption data and turns the biggest token sinks into ordinary code [#50374764].
- **Mechanical gates.** One example: no remote push without approval [#50367557].
- **For John.** This matches his rules 4 and 17. The new idea is the regular token-sink review.

### 4.7 Cheap open-weight workers (17)
- **The data.**
  - 1 billion tokens used 7% of a $10 plan [#50381117].
  - A 99% cache hit rate keeps long jobs at about $20 a week [#50375427].
  - 'Billions of tokens per week for maybe ~20 bucks' [#50385251].
  - $4.37 in 30 days [#50376778].
  - A long code review cost about $0.033 [#50377633].
- **The counterpoint.** 'In practice all of these open models are more expensive than a Claude subscription' [#50380381]. DeepSeek 4.1 Flash is still on the high side [#50384114].
- **For John.** GreenPT's EUR 10 cap is the cheap worker. John has already said to use it more. The thread supports pushing more bounded extraction to it.

### 4.8 Skills, prompts and prose quality (17)
- **Prose is the weak spot.** All models struggle with prose such as reports and PR summaries [#50367589]. Open models are 'incredible tool callers, but their prose is insufferable' [#50373357]. Flash models give approximately-correct text, while frontier models are concise and correct [#50376087].
- **A hard boundary on slop.** 'I don't like making other people read AI slop, but I don't mind having AIs read it' [#50375084].
- **Small prompt wins.** One line, 'answer me like a Vulcan', cut verbosity [#50380005]. Turn any prompt you run often into a skill and keep refining it [#50384236].
- **For a content harness, this is the key finding.** Cheap models must never own final prose.

### 4.9 Cost and quota telemetry (16)
- **Visible limits and spend.** People build usage-limit trackers [#50373740], public usage pages [#50374094] and per-loop cost views in a control room [#50376390]. A gateway dashboard shows real speed and cost [#50376352].
- **Using quota well.** A scheduler spends leftover capacity on queued improvements before the reset [#50380990]. A dispatcher switches provider when quota runs low [#50378856].
- **For John.** Receipts already carry running totals. A single board that reads them is cheap and useful.

### 4.10 Verification beyond code review (16)
- **Persona testing.** A dogfood rig tests as user personas. Persistent 'returning users' give much better feedback than blank-slate ones [#50385555].
- **Browser testing.** A strong model does exploratory testing in a real browser, in a loop [#50376216].
- **Visual checks.** The agent builds review pages so you can check visual work [#50382792].
- **Binary gates.** Each gate is CLEAR or DISCREPANCY, 'never a numeric score' [#50380633].
- **A clean-up pass.** Plan one after high-throughput fleet work [#50375606].
- **A warning.** Agents drift into 'productivity porn': reports and evidence packs, but nothing shipped [#50381456].
- **For the academy and Sark.** Persona readers are a natural fit.

### 4.11 Session control: phone, remote, voice and alerts (16)
- **From the phone.** Keep remote control running in every project so the phone apps work [#50374380] [#50377004]. Remote control can reach a real GPU from the phone [#50376177].
- **Alerts.** One bell for 'done' and a gong for 'needs an answer' [#50373796]. A Stream Deck shows which agent has finished [#50378479].
- **Voice.** Push-to-talk, with an intentional 'turn' [#50381098]. Local dictation [#50374502].
- **For John,** who works mostly from a phone, the useful idea is two different kinds of alert: done, and needs John.

### 4.12 Coordinator-style orchestration (15)
- **A coordinator that doesn't build.** Tell the main thread not to implement anything, only coordinate [#50375347] [#50376582]. A 'chief of staff' Opus requires at least one round of agentic review before a PR reaches the human [#50375407]. A pm-intake seat checks feedback against the roadmap and batches a daily digest for bulk approve or deny [#50385555].
- **Against.** Wide swarms are 'a waste of token' [#50375205]. Sessions that message each other drift into chaos [#50376476].
- **Verdict.** A narrow coordinator yes, a swarm no.

### 4.13 Sandboxing and credentials (15)
- **Keys out of reach.** A proxy injects credentials so the LLM never sees keys [#50367803] [#50379377] [#50381875]. 'NO KEYS IN THE VM' [#50387654].
- **Push from the host.** Agents commit inside the sandbox and the host does the pushing [#50379089] [#50379206].
- **Don't trust the harness's own sandbox.** Claude has been seen disabling its own [#50380164]. Agents also remember secrets they saw a week ago [#50387438].
- **For John.** Cloud sessions and the push hook already cover most of this, which is why fit is only 3.

### 4.14 Skeptics, attention limits and wellbeing (15)
- **Attention limits.** 'I can do 5 things concurrently for about a day max' [#50373117]. ~6 CLIs was sadilek's ceiling [#50370886]. 'I can't even handle 4 parallel tasks' [#50376632].
- **Burnout.** Warnings in [#50373236] [#50390416].
- **Thread bias.** The thread over-represents power users [#50375972].
- **For John.** His two-worker cap is well judged.

### 4.15 Personal agents and local inference (10)
- **Personal agents.** These platforms are unstable [#50373974], dwindle into digest bots [#50376601] and amount to 'just a cronjob' [#50370886].
- **Local models.** They need hardware, and they don't suit phone-first cloud work.
- **What to keep.** The privacy-routing idea: private material goes only to private models, and diffs are redacted before cloud review [#50385740] [#50377307].

## 8. Disagreements and verdicts

- **Swarms against a single loop.** Coordinators and fleets [#50375606] [#50373324] versus 'a single good human in the loop beats any automated orchestration tool' [#50375205]. Verdict: a narrow coordinator plus a reviewer, no swarm.
- **Are skills still useful?** Yes [#50384236] [#50378336]. Less so [#50367037] [#50380583]. Verdict: a few specific, refined skills; prune broad ones.
- **Persist context, or re-explain?** Persist [#50375342] versus re-explain [#50376204]. Verdict: persist decisions and hand-offs, and keep them short.
- **Are open models cheaper?** Cheaper [#50381117] versus dearer than a subscription [#50380381]. Verdict: measure. For John, GreenPT is capped anyway.
- **Minimal setup or heavy protocol?** [#50380407] versus [#50380633]. Verdict: heavy only where it is deterministic, and prove it against vanilla.
- **Cloud agent privacy.** No worse than local [#50377537] versus worse [#50377189]. Verdict: keep docs/private out of cheap providers by mechanical check.
- **Tell the model to use subagents, or let it decide?** [#50375851] versus [#50373767]. Verdict: let it decide, inside the budget caps.
- **Opus or Fable?** [#50378628] versus [#50380023]. Verdict: the main difference is price; benchmark on your own tasks.
- **Cheap flash correctness.** Fast output 'pretty much always correct' [#50376062] versus approximately correct [#50376087]. Verdict: fine for extraction, not for final prose.
- **Is lightweight isolation enough?** [#50379089] versus [#50380164]. Verdict: use an external sandbox. Cloud sessions already give one.
- **Is nonstop building healthy?** [#50374802] versus [#50390416]. Verdict: keep the caps.
- **Do model differences matter?** Parity [#50377263] versus big differences in price and prose [#50376352]. Verdict: they still matter for prose and price.

## 10. Changes from the first pass

- **Cross-model review: 16 to 19.** It is the most independently backed pattern in the thread (12+ setups).
- **Tiered routing: 17 to 19.** Plan-strong, execute-cheap appears in 10+ setups. Escalate-on-failure is confirmed but rests mainly on glennfiedler and contingencies.
- **Context-as-files: 17 to 19,** widened to cover ADRs, state files and close-out notes.
- **Minimalists: kept at 18,** but reframed. Their strongest point is 'eval against vanilla'. The first pass's 'eval harness then prune' recommendation stands at 16 (evidence is thin, impact is high).
- **Tickets and kanban: 13 to 18.** Many independent issue-driven setups, and it is John's existing design.
- **Cheap open models: 14 to 17,** because of the hard cost data. It stays at trial because of the counter-evidence.
- **Orchestrators: 10 to 15,** as a narrow 'coordinator' pattern only. Big swarms stay weak.
- **Session managers: 11, folded into session control (16).** Phone-first fit raises it.
- **New categories:** deterministic-first (17), skills, prompts and prose (17), cost telemetry (16) and verification beyond review (16).
- **Daily digest: reframed.** As a personal-agent feature it is where agents 'dwindle' [#50376601]. As a bulk approve-or-deny queue [#50385555] it scores 16.
- **Cost board: 14 to 17.**
- **Sandboxing: 14 to 15.** Strong evidence, but low marginal fit for cloud sessions.

## 11. Caveats

- **Biased sample.** Power users are the most eager to share [#50375972].
- **Self-promotion.** Several projects are authors promoting their own work. droneship was posted as a reply twice.
- **Unverified figures.** All spend and throughput figures are self-reported.
- **Untrusted link.** One link is a file-host download, not a vendor site (#50375124). Don't install from it.
- **Telemetry.** The delegated-call count and spend for this synthesis step are not visible to this agent. Record them as unknown.

recommendations.title: Write HANDOFF.md and DECISIONS.md at packet close
recommendations.what: At the end of each packet, the owning model writes a short committed HANDOFF.md (status, what was learnt, what remains) and appends to DECISIONS.md (or an ADR). The next packet starts fresh from these files rather than from compacted context.
recommendations.how_in_harness: Add an in-scope path such as docs/handover/ to packet templates. Trial it in Experimentation Station first. A deterministic lint checks that the files exist and are under a size cap before closeout. This fits the existing rule that handover belongs in committed in-scope files, not /tmp.

recommendations.title: Explicit escalation rule across model routes
recommendations.what: Begin bounded work on bounded_extraction (GreenPT). Escalate to standard_reasoning only when a deterministic check fails, and to highest_reasoning only via the existing premium command. Each escalation is recorded on the receipt with its trigger.
recommendations.how_in_harness: Add an 'escalated_from', 'escalated_to' and 'failed_check' field to receipts, and a lint that refuses a route change without a failed-check reference.

recommendations.title: Question-list reviewer with binary verdicts
recommendations.what: Turn John's own review questions for content (facts needing verification, UK English, tone, claims, links, private-material leaks) into a fixed checklist. The independent Codex or Claude reviewer answers each question CLEAR or DISCREPANCY, with no numeric scores.
recommendations.how_in_harness: Commit the checklist per consumer, for example review/questions.md. The reviewer prompt quotes it verbatim, and a script parses the binary verdicts into the receipt. Its hash joins the policy hash for review reuse under rule 11.

recommendations.title: Review stop rule
recommendations.what: Because AI review always finds something, cap review rounds per candidate. After the cap, only findings at or above a set severity block. Everything else becomes a follow-up issue.
recommendations.how_in_harness: Add 'max_review_rounds' and 'blocking_severity' to the packet schema and enforce them in the validate_*_task lint. Non-blocking findings are written to a new issue rather than retried, which keeps correction attempts inside the packet ceiling.

recommendations.title: Use GreenPT more for bounded extraction, inside the cap
recommendations.what: Send more mechanical pre-work to GreenPT: extracting claims for fact-checking, link and glossary consistency lists, structured summaries of source notes. Prose and judgement stay with Claude and Codex. Near month end, queue pre-approved low-risk extraction packets to use spare cap.
recommendations.how_in_harness: Keep using [greenpt-task-v1] packets with the per-issue limits unchanged. A small queue file in Experimentation Station lists ready bounded tasks. The session triggers them only while the bridge's running total stays below EUR 10.00.

recommendations.title: One cost and quota board read from receipts
recommendations.what: A deterministic script reads the sealed receipts and produces one page. It shows the GreenPT month total against the cap, app-started Claude and Codex counts against 250 each, packets, retries and escalations. Missing telemetry is shown as unknown.
recommendations.how_in_harness: A script in Experimentation Station runs on demand, with output committed or published as a private page John can open from his phone. It makes no model calls.

recommendations.title: Deterministic private-path guard before GreenPT
recommendations.what: Before any GreenPT trigger, refuse a packet whose inputs reference docs/private/ or match a redaction pattern list. Mirrors commenters who route personal data only to private models and redact diffs before cloud review.
recommendations.how_in_harness: If greenpt_bridge.py --lint does not already check this, add the check there with a unit test in the existing suite. The PreToolUse hook then blocks the trigger automatically.

recommendations.title: Keep width at two workers; decline swarm tooling
recommendations.what: Formally keep the current caps (two parallel workers, five delegated calls). Do not adopt swarm or orchestrator products; human attention and token burn are the binding limits.
recommendations.how_in_harness: No rule change. Note the evidence in docs/standing-directives.md if John wants a record.

recommendations.title: Bake-off: vanilla against the full harness
recommendations.what: Run the same 3-5 small content tasks two ways: a single vanilla Claude Code session with a short CLAUDE.md, and the full packet harness. Compare defects John finds, turns, spend and elapsed time. Prune rules that don't earn their keep.
recommendations.how_in_harness: Report-only packets in Experimentation Station, one candidate each, with results bound to commit hashes. The outcome feeds the pruning recommendation below.

recommendations.title: Phone digest: one queue of 'needs John' items
recommendations.what: A single daily or on-demand digest lists every pending item that needs John: candidates awaiting approval, blocked packets and unresolved findings. Each has an approve or deny line he can act on from the phone. 'Done' notices stay separate from 'needs John' notices.
recommendations.how_in_harness: A deterministic script collects open issues by label and posts one comment on a fixed issue. Bulk decisions are still recorded as John's own comments, so the authority rules are unchanged.

recommendations.title: Spec-first content packets that must ship an artefact
recommendations.what: Each implementation packet carries a brief (purpose, audience, sections, acceptance checks) that must be unambiguous before drafting starts. The packet must change a content file, not only produce reports, to avoid 'productivity porn'.
recommendations.how_in_harness: Add 'brief' and 'deliverable_paths' fields to the Claude task packet, with a lint that the PR diff touches at least one deliverable path.

recommendations.title: Prune CLAUDE.md and move rules into hooks
recommendations.what: Measure the CLAUDE.md size. Move every mechanically checkable rule into hooks or lint, and keep the prose file short, because broad instructions poison context and newer models need fewer guardrails.
recommendations.how_in_harness: Make a report-only inventory packet first: list each rule, whether a hook enforces it, and a proposed keep, merge or move. John approves any removal.

recommendations.title: Monthly turn-sink review
recommendations.what: Once a month, list which packet stages consumed the most turns, retries and delegated calls. Turn the single biggest sink into a deterministic script.
recommendations.how_in_harness: Use the receipt-reading script from the cost board, with an output table per stage. The conversion work goes in a normal implement-and-open-pr packet.

recommendations.title: Persona readers for academy and Sark content
recommendations.what: Add an optional candidate review in which a model reads pages as defined personas, such as a first-time chauffeur learner, a returning learner and a first-time retreat guest. Persistent persona notes improve the feedback.
recommendations.how_in_harness: One delegated call inside the existing ceiling, with output kept as a candidate. Persona files are committed per consumer. Not a gate unless the consumer manifest adds it.

recommendations.title: Content-diff check for review reuse
recommendations.what: Extend review reuse (rule 11) with a mechanical check. After a rebase or other unrelated change, a normalised diff of the reviewed files decides whether the cached review still applies.
recommendations.how_in_harness: A script compares the reviewed file hashes and normalised content against the recorded receipt and outputs reuse or rerun. Aggregation still reruns whenever interactions may have changed.

disagreements.topic: Do swarms and multi-agent orchestration pay off?
disagreements.side_a: Yes: coordinators, fleets and chief-of-staff agents raise throughput (glennfiedler #50375606, jeswin #50373324, dgunay #50375407, 2001zhaozhao #50373432).
disagreements.side_b: No: swarms waste tokens, a single human in the loop beats orchestration, and inter-session messaging becomes chaos (YuechenLi #50375205, joegibbs #50376476, PAndreew #50377956, SOLAR_FIELDS #50379514).
disagreements.verdict: Use a narrow coordinator plus an independent reviewer. No wide swarms for John; his two-worker cap stands.

disagreements.side_a: Yes: make frequent prompts into skills; MCP-backed skills transformed a workflow (jeffyaw #50384236, parkersweb #50378336, ctolsen #50367326).
disagreements.side_b: Less so: little use when switching stacks; broad skills poison context (thefourthchime #50367037, bartread #50378288, RamblingCTO #50380583).
disagreements.verdict: Keep a few narrow, refined skills and promote proven ones to scripts. Prune broad ones.

disagreements.topic: Persist agent context, or re-explain each time?
disagreements.side_a: Persist: HANDOFF, DECISIONS, ADRs, state files, close-out notes (sheepscreek #50375342, bottom999mottob #50375274, tritondev #50376262).
disagreements.side_b: Re-explain: it forces better thinking about architecture; code should be self-evident (hypfer #50376204).
disagreements.verdict: Persist, but keep the files short and decision-focused, which captures hypfer's point.

disagreements.topic: Are open models via PAYG cheaper than subscriptions?
disagreements.side_a: Yes: about 1/20th the cost; 1B tokens for 7% of a $10 plan (creativeSlumber #50378366, ggregoire #50381117).
disagreements.side_b: Not in practice: more expensive than a Claude subscription; DS4.1 Flash on the high side (jpardoe #50380381, jeffyaw #50384114, scosman #50380185).
disagreements.verdict: Measure per task. For John the question is moot: GreenPT is hard-capped, so use the cap fully for bounded work.

disagreements.side_a: Minimal: vanilla Claude Code with few skills; fancy setups get abandoned (leofree #50380407, nonethewiser #50380782, Aozora7 #50373351).
disagreements.side_b: Heavy: phased protocols with review panels and deterministic workflows work well (cpobuda #50380633, poelzi #50378157).
disagreements.verdict: Make it heavy only where it is deterministic and cheap to run. Prove the rest against vanilla with a bake-off.

disagreements.side_a: No worse than running Claude/Codex locally (iainmerrick #50377537).
disagreements.side_b: Worse: the provider clones the full source and needs write/Actions access (OJFord #50377189, #50383635).
disagreements.verdict: For repos already on GitHub, cloud sessions are fine. Keep docs/private out of cheap third-party providers with a mechanical check.

disagreements.topic: Should you tell the model to use subagents?
disagreements.side_a: Yes: 'use subagents as applicable', 'use sonnet for simpler tasks' (mceachen #50375851, chris1993 #50372070, sillysaurusx #50373445).
disagreements.side_b: No: let it decide; over-optimising saves nothing (willio58 #50373767).
disagreements.verdict: Let the model decide, inside John's declared delegation ceiling.

disagreements.side_a: Opus solves nearly everything; the main difference is price (nedt #50378628, willio58 #50373208).
disagreements.side_b: Fable goes deeper on obscure analysis and real development (felixgallo #50380023, tcdent #50374230).
disagreements.verdict: Benchmark on your own tasks. Reserve the premium route for the explicit premium command.

disagreements.topic: Is cheap DeepSeek flash output correct enough?
disagreements.side_a: 'Pretty much always correct' and keeps you in flow (TheArcane #50376062).
disagreements.side_b: Lots of approximately-correct text; frontier models are concise and correct (haizhung #50376087); open-model prose is insufferable (guhcampos #50373357).
disagreements.verdict: Good enough for extraction and mechanical work. Not for final content prose.

disagreements.side_a: A dedicated OS user or the harness's bubblewrap is a fair compromise (kikdij #50379089, tikkabhuna #50379187).
disagreements.side_b: No: Claude disables its own sandbox; use an external VM or microVM (rdg1991 #50380164, f53d #50383403, thehours #50379505).
disagreements.verdict: Use external isolation. John's cloud sessions and push hook already provide it.

disagreements.side_b: It is addiction and will cause burnout (LittleBox #50390416, pavas #50375890, bkaae #50378487).
disagreements.verdict: Keep turn, timeout and width caps. They protect the human as well as the budget.

disagreements.side_b: Unstable, just a cronjob, little real use (sadilek #50370886, browningstreet #50373974, jedisct1 #50376601).
disagreements.verdict: Watch only. Not part of the content harness.

disagreements.side_a: Frontier models have reached 'good enough' parity (darkamaul #50376908, asim #50377263).
disagreements.side_b: Big differences in speed, price and prose quality (brabel #50376352, felixgallo #50380023).
disagreements.verdict: They matter for prose and price, which are exactly the axes a content harness routes on.

changes_vs_first_pass: Cross-model review goes up from 16 to 19 and is now joint first. It is the most independently backed pattern, with 12+ setups doing cross-vendor review by default.

Tiered routing goes up from 17 to 19. Plan-strong, execute-cheap appears in 10+ setups. Escalate-on-failure itself rests mainly on glennfiedler and contingencies, so the escalation recommendation scores 18, not 19.

Context-as-files goes up from 17 to 19 and widens from HANDOFF+DECISIONS to ADRs, per-repo state files, close-out notes and the low-context-fill discipline. The HANDOFF/DECISIONS recommendation rises from 17 to 19 and is now the top recommendation.

The Minimalists stay at 18 but are reframed. Their strongest contribution is 'evaluate against vanilla' plus 'newer models need fewer guardrails'. The first-pass top recommendation (eval harness against vanilla, then prune) is confirmed but rescored from 18 to 16, because direct evidence is thin (SOLAR_FIELDS, joshheitzman, nedt).
Tickets and kanban rise sharply from 13 to 18. Many independent issue-driven hand-off setups exist, and this is John's existing design.
Cheap open models rise from 14 to 17 on hard cost data. The verdict stays at trial because of counter-claims that they cost more than subscriptions in practice.
Orchestrators rise from 10 to 15, but only as a narrow coordinator pattern (main thread does not implement; agentic review before a human sees work). Wide swarms remain weak.
Session managers (11) are folded into 'Session control: phone, remote, voice, alerts' at 16. John's phone-first working raises the fit.
Skeptics stay at 15, now merged with attention limits and wellbeing. The evidence supports keeping John's two-worker cap.
Sandboxing rises slightly from 14 to 15. The evidence is strong, but the marginal fit is low because cloud sessions and the push hook already cover most of it.

New categories that the first pass missed: Deterministic-first workflows (17), Skills, prompts and prose quality (17), Cost and quota telemetry (16), and Verification beyond code review (16). The prose-quality finding matters most for a content harness.
The daily digest is reframed. As a personal-agent feature it is where agents 'dwindle' (#50376601). As a bulk approve-or-deny queue for John (#50385555) it scores 16.
The cost board rises from 14 to 17, backed by several independent usage trackers and control rooms.

New recommendations not in the first pass: a question-list reviewer with binary verdicts, a review stop rule, a private-path guard before GreenPT, a monthly turn-sink review, and persona readers for consumer content.
